correctness.rationale: For fixed preassigned edges, infection-time layers are directed BFS layers. With original peak 1 each unique layer vertex is a cut vertex for later distance layers; otherwise a strict increase needs a vaccinated layer of at least three vertices at distance at least three, requiring six survivors and one vaccine recipient, so n>=7. The seven-vertex example has exact layers {0},{1,2},{3,4},{5,6} before deletion and {0},{1},{3},{4,5,6} after. Exhaustive 128/128 edge-subset census yields p^2(p^5-2p^4+3p^3-1), with a unique root as the fifth-degree factor derivative is p^2(5p^2-8p+9)>0 for p>0. Standalone verify.py execution passed, including 20,000 supplemental random small graphs; randomness is not the proof of the universal bound.

value.rationale: Peak concurrent infections quantify a health-service-capacity observable independent from infection risk and epidemic termination time. A universal, sharp minimal-population cutoff in arbitrary directed graphs is a natural finite structural classification. A minimal seven-person witness has a nontrivial exact stochastic phase threshold under homogeneous transmissibility; its exhaustive 128-case table and monotone quintic distinguish rare-contact protection from high-contact peak amplification. This is mathematically motivated without claiming policy applicability.
